summary: This is a real follow-up to combo-wg-occ2 and the mechanism is measurable, but the register plan as written cannot build: producer 24 / consumers 112 needs 31744 registers per CTA, which is more than the 80x384 = 30720 launch pool, and 88 registers at launch breaks the 2-CTA register file. Proceed only with the register fix and a gate that covers all the judge draws. Expect at most -1% on verify_32, so read the result from the prepare prints and profile rows, not from the headline.
justification:
A. MECHANISM (plausible but smaller than claimed). The combo run printed this for the B256 judge rebuild (draw 4), in hypotheses/archive/combo-wg-occ2-v64-hot-interleave-align2/*.log: 23/32 experts touched, max 256 routes on one expert, 26 chunks at V64 vs 24 at s5 (s5 is OCC1 and cuts every 128 rows). So NMAX 128 removes 2 of 26 chunk-columns of items, about 7.7% of the w13 dequant work. It does not change the wgmma work. The hypothesis's '~130 routes, 3 -> 2 chunks' is one draw's picture; the hottest draw is 4 -> 2. The 'read from DRAM 2-3 times' part is mostly wrong: V64s/V64 = 0.997 on the judge rebuild, so the item order does not change L2 behavior and the duplicate reads cost little at the DRAM level. What is left is duplicate dequant. DIAGNOSIS action 3 and b128-n32-deep-ring say the consumer is dequant/serial-bound at about 2 TB/s (w13 V64 1.98 TB/s on the judge rebuild), so that is the right lever. The realistic ceiling is about 5-7% of the 219-225 us w13 row, roughly -10 to -15 us, before costs. The -11 to -22 us estimate is optimistic.
WEAKEST LINK, part 1 (fatal as written): the register arithmetic. Geo2's static_assert (RDEC*128 + RINC*256 <= REGS*THREADS) with REGS = 80 rejects 24/112: 31744 > 30720. Launch registers come in steps of 8, and 88 x 384 x 2 = 67584 > 65536. So 112 consumer registers at OCC2 with 384 threads is impossible. The build fails at the static_assert, or, if someone relaxes the assert, setmaxnreg.inc hangs and the check is charged as a timeout. The only feasible split is 32/104 (or 24/104). That leaves 104 - 64 accumulators - 16 a[4][4] = 24 registers for descriptors, pointers, scales, loop state and the epilogue, so a spill is likely.
WEAKEST LINK, part 2: in the judge routing, about 22 of 24 chunks are not split. Every one of them pays N128's costs and gains nothing: STG 2 instead of 3 (weight bytes in flight per CTA drop from 27 KB to 18 KB), and two wait<0> groups per stage instead of one. The saving lands only on the 1-2 hot experts. The net could be zero or negative.
Shape expectations: bs=256 faster and bs=128 flat are consistent. B128 stays Marlin, and its judge rebuild has max 44 routes with no splits. +0.5-1.0% headline is below the ±1.5% CI, as the file admits.
PRIOR: correctly named. combo-wg-occ2-v64-hot-interleave-align2 ran NMAX 64 / STG 3 on both kernels, and its reviewer suggested exactly this as an unminted follow-up (DIAGNOSIS action 5). Not a do-not-try item: the dropped b256-n64-deep-ring was about bytes in flight, and this is about deduplicating dequant. Smem is checked and fits: 1024 + 2x41984 + 18432 = 103424 B dynamic, plus 8192 static and 1 KB reserve = 112640 B, x2 = 225280 <= 233472.
confounders: restack-occ2-wg2-b256-two-stream-halves-on-master (depends_on; queued, not landed): master has no wg2_kernel today (submission.py has only s5 with setmaxnreg 40/232), so 'base: master' cannot be built tonight. It must be built on the restack branch, or on the combo branch hyp/muse_moe_w4a16/combo-wg-occ2-v64-hot-interleave-align2 (8550d0f4). Its result is then relative to that base, not to master's 1.3866.

wg-pdl-gather-w13-w2-chain (landed f7eac2c3): PDL across the wgmma chain overlaps w13's tail with w2's launch. N128 makes the hot expert's items about 2x longer and changes the last-wave tail, so any change in the w13 row is partly a PDL/tail interaction. Check whether the restack carries PDL onto wg2; if it does not, a tail change is pure scheduling.

align-two-phase-port-from17 (landed a0e52640) plus the combo's F2 front end: the device chunk cut runs on block_experts from align2 at bsm 16. NMAX 128 only changes the cut (8 blocks), so this is not a numeric confounder, but the _wg_chunks host mirror must use cut = 8 for the new instantiation or the printed chunk counts will be wrong.
interference: No companion is warranted. Both a gain and a loss can be attributed in one run if the prepare selector times these on the same judge-rebuild routings with interleaved cold-L2 graphs: V64 (base), N128 (new), and a print-only V64r. V64r is NMAX 64 / STG 3 with the same per-record dequant and two wait<0> groups per stage, which isolates what the restructure costs from what the deduplication saves. It also needs to print chunks, w13 kernel-only microseconds and TB/s per candidate. N128 vs V64r is the dedup effect; V64r vs V64 is the restructure cost. That is free in-run, so a separate ab-revert or ab-tune check would buy nothing. The landed items above do not need reverting to read the w13 row. The open question about the queued wg2-pingpong-consumers-occ2-b256 (it changes the same consumer loop) is about ordering, not about a companion: if pingpong lands first, re-base onto it, because its register split will compete for the same 104.
rules_flags: No precision or caching issue: NVFP4 is still dequantized in registers, accumulation is fp32, and h is bf16 as before.

Hang risk, not a rules break: if the 24/112 split is forced past the static_assert, setmaxnreg.inc deadlocks and the 15-minute run limit charges a timeout. Keep master's rule that numRegs != 80, localSizeBytes != 0, occupancy < 2 or any ptxas spill turns the variant OFF before its first launch.
_wg_judge_ids must stay a ported rebuild of the generate_input logic, not an import of reference.py (an imported reference is rejected).

Gate strength conflicts with today's lesson: a single round >= 1.02x is what mis-routed bf16 today. Use two interleaved rounds, each >= 1.03x (or >= 1.02x with an IQR bound that excludes 1.0), on the worse routing.
open_questions: REQUIRED EDIT 1: replace 24/112. Options: (a) keep 32/104 with N128 accumulators plus a[4][4], and accept OFF if ptxas reports any spill; (b) drop setmaxnreg and use a 288-thread CTA (2 consumer warpgroups plus 1 producer warp), __launch_bounds__(288, 2), 112 registers uniform (112 x 288 x 2 = 64512 <= 65536), if the producer path allows it. State which, and keep a static_assert on the pool.

REQUIRED EDIT 2: gate on the worse of several judge-rebuild draws (at least the draw with the 256-route expert and a draw without a split), not on one draw plus zipf a=0.9. Under no-split routings N128 is pure cost (STG 2, two waits), and the judge varies its draws. Print per draw: chunks for V64 and N128, w13 microseconds and TB/s.

Correct the expected rows: hot experts are 3-4 chunks -> 2 depending on the draw (26 -> 24 total chunks on draw 4), and DRAM re-read is not the mechanism (V64s/V64 = 0.997). Restate the target as w13 <= ~210 us on the judge rebuild, about -4% on that row.

Can N128 be confined to hot-expert items? For example, launch N128 only over experts with more than 64 routes and V64 over the rest on two streams, or split by bucket, so the non-split chunks keep STG 3. This would remove the main cost on the roughly 22 non-split chunks.
Does the restack branch carry wg-pdl onto wg2? This decides how much of a w13-row change is tail interaction.
